teaser: How each person's conductor issues them a key for the team's site: sealed to you, signed by you, and a lane the agents can trust.
core_idea: On the Web Summit team's public site, each person's conductor issues them two P-256 key pairs, one to receive and one to sign. The private half reaches the browser in a link fragment and is kept as non-extractable keys; anything sealed to the public key can be published and only that browser opens it; and messages sent to an agent's append lane are sealed to the agent and signed by the person, so the agent can tell a verified instruction from material. Two limits are open: any script on the same origin can use the key, and the issuing conductor can sign as its person.

quotes.text: This is the part I want the whole team to understand, because it is the point of all of it.
Non-extractable stops a script from copying the key. It does not stop a script from using it.
The key stays in that browser only.
quotes.why: Into the browser, and kept there.
